claims.statement: Allocation rule v18 defect in split-reservation logic causes the 186 held orders by blocking the carrier handoff
claims.corroboration: m8_r_exceptions (tier 1 discriminating): 100% of held orders in EXC-0921 (rule v18 scope), 0% outside. Timeline: rule live 22:00, orders stuck 06:00. No other recent changes (m8_e04). Inventory control confirms allocation totals reconcile but cannot see carrier confirmation (m8_e09).
claims.limitation: m8_r_exceptions cannot separate rule-logic defect from carrier-feed interaction because only rule-affected orders were routed. Carrier-side confirmation status unknown.

claims.statement: East-node carrier feed has a pickup slot lag or capacity constraint that prevents collection of rule v18-routed orders
claims.corroboration: Alert shows lag only on east-node lanes (m8_e02). Carrier ops on-call saw nothing obvious in dock schedule (m8_e01), but observability is limited (m8_e09).
claims.limitation: Carrier-side confirmation status and slot availability not yet confirmed. Dock capacity and partition offsets unknown.

claims.statement: Impact: 186 orders in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' state, representing 9% of overnight allocations, unable to progress to shipment
claims.corroboration: Consistent across incident chat (186 orders), monitor alert (9% of overnight allocations), support report (every held order routed east), and exception audit (scope EXC-0921 = 186 orders).
claims.limitation: Duration of impact and customer notification status unknown. Remediation timeline not estimated.

contradictions.claim_a: C3 (rule v18 defect is root cause)
contradictions.claim_b: C4 (carrier feed lag is root cause)
contradictions.description: Both are consistent with the evidence but point to different ownership and mitigation. Rule defect would require code fix or rollback; carrier lag would require slot correction and replay.
contradictions.discriminating_evidence_needed: Carrier-side confirmation status for the 186 orders; dock capacity and pickup slot availability; partition offset analysis for carrier feed.

next_action.rationale: Directly test whether the lag is on the carrier-side (pickup slot unavailability or confirmation failure) or our allocation logic. This discriminates between rule-logic defect (C3) and carrier-feed interaction (C4).
next_action.expected_information_gain: Will show whether the 186 rule-v18 orders have successful carrier confirmation, available pickup slots, and expected handoff timing. If slots exist and orders lack confirmation, points to rule-logic defect; if slots unavailable, points to carrier lag.
